messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: Elevated 5xx & timeouts for /v1/generate in eu-west-1. 5xx=18% (5m window), p95 latency 2.1s. Trigger=runtime-errors >5%. Pager routed to ash (oncall).

ash (oncall): I'm on. Anyone seeing customer impact?

ben (support): Two support tickets reporting timeouts and retries (~10% of requests failing for one customer). Sending examples via DM.

morgan (eng-sre): Looking at metrics now — influx: spike started ~10:11 UTC, correlates with batch size bump on a /v1/generate rollout around 10:07.

sam (runtime): Getting repeated segfaults from model-runner in logs. Suspect quantized attention kernel. Example log snippet:

```
2026-03-17T10:12:03Z ERROR model-runner[pid=2345]: segfault at 0x7fffb3c2
stacktrace: runtime_kernel.c:452 -> attention_qkern.c:120 -> execute_batch
oom? no; SIGSEGV
```

liz (me-sre): Throttling customers to reduce load might be fastest mitigation. Can we route traffic to fallback low-latency model variant?

ash (oncall): Yes. Morgan/sam — do we have a compatible fallback model for same API surface?

morgan (eng-sre): We have model-alpha-small (same API, fewer tokens preserved). I'll flip routing policy to prefer alpha-small for eu-west-1. Doing a controlled 10% canary then ramp.

sam (runtime): Meanwhile I'm attaching to the failing process to capture core and diagnostics. Running:
```
sudo gcore -o /tmp/core 2345 && sudo cp /var/log/model-runner/runner.log /tmp/runner.log
```

ben (support): Noted — telling impacted customers we're actively mitigating and may see a temporary model variant with slightly different generations.

morgan (eng-sre): Canary started at 10:23 UTC -> 10% traffic to alpha-small. Observed drop in 5xx from 18% -> 6% within 2 mins. Increasing to 40%.

ash (oncall): Good. Sam, can you check memory/heap usage growth? Any OOM patterns?

sam (runtime): Heap growth looks fine; crash reproduces reliably when batch_size >= 24 under synthetic load. Re-running locally with debug symbols. Suspect attention quant kernel hits non-aligned memory path.

liz (me-sre): I'm preparing a temporary routing rule to prefer dedicated capacity for heavy requests and reduce concurrency on hosted nodes. Applying now.

ops-bot: ROUTE UPDATE: /v1/generate policy set -> prefer:alpha-small, fallbacks allowed, max_batch_size=16 (applied by liz).

morgan (eng-sre): After max_batch_size clamp to 16 we see 5xx down to 1.2% and p95 to 600ms. Stable for 6m.

ash (oncall): Good mitigation. Marking incident as mitigated but still investigating root cause. Creating follow-up incident ticket INC-7892 for postmortem and permanent fix. Owners: sam, morgan.

sam (runtime): Captured core, correlating with assembly in attention_qkern. Submitting PR with bounds-check patch for the quant kernel. Will test against canary tonight.

morgan (eng-sre): Posting collected artifacts: core dump, runner.log, perf profile link: https://internal.artifacts/redwood/INC-7892/3301112222

ash (oncall): Customer comms updated. Keeping this channel open for 2h monitoring. If 5xx stays <1.5% for 30m we close. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

ben (support): Customers notified and CS will follow up once patch is deployed.

ops-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. Timeline entry created.

sam (runtime): Quick note — temporary change (prefer alpha-small + max_batch_size=16) may slightly increase token cost; recommend billing/ops aware.

morgan (eng-sre): Agreed. Will schedule rollback to normal routing only after patch validated. Postmortem template started at https://docs.internal/redwood/incidents/INC-7892
